script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Morning, Sarah. Today is November 14th, 2026. Can't believe it's already mid-November. Need more coffee.
script.ja: サラさん、おはようございます。今日は2026年11月14日ですね。もう11月の半ばなんて信じられないです。もっとコーヒーが必要だ。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Good morning, Alex. Yes, the days are flying by. I'm on my second cup of tea already.
script.ja: アレックス、おはよう。ええ、あっという間に日が過ぎるわね。私はもう紅茶を2杯目よ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Two cups? Wow. I jump at everything these days. Pretty sure it's the baby. And lack of sleep.
script.ja: 2杯ですか？すごいな。最近はなんでも飛び起きちゃうんです。きっと赤ちゃんのせいだ。それに寝不足も。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It sounds about right. Anyway, did you see the weather forecast? It's overcast today, but no rain.
script.ja: そうでしょうね。ところで、天気予報見た？今日は曇りだけど、雨は降らないみたいよ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Oh, good. I didn't check. High of 18 degrees, right? It's getting pretty chilly in the evenings.
script.ja: ああ、よかった。見てなかったんです。最高気温18度くらいでしたっけ？夜はかなり肌寒くなってきましたよね。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Yes, around 18.2 degrees for the high, and 10.8 for the low. Rain probability is only 4 percent.
script.ja: ええ、最高が18.2度くらいで、最低が10.8度。雨の確率はたった4パーセントよ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: That's good. I hate carrying an umbrella if I don't have to. Did you catch any of the news this morning?
script.ja: それはいいですね。必要ないなら傘を持ち歩くのは嫌いです。今朝、何かニュース見ましたか？

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: A little. There was that M5.7 earthquake in central Japan early Sunday. Over 20 injured in Aichi and Shizuoka.
script.ja: 少しだけ。日曜の早朝に、中部地方でM5.7の地震があったでしょう。愛知と静岡で20人以上が負傷したって。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Oh, I heard about that. That's terrible. I feel like I read about a decent-sized earthquake every year around this time.
script.ja: ああ、それ聞きました。大変でしたね。毎年この時期にそこそこの地震のニュースを読んでいる気がします。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It's certainly a worry, isn't it? Especially with older buildings.
script.ja: 確かに心配事よね。特に古い建物なんかは。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Yeah. My wife gets really worried. We should probably review our emergency kit again. It's been a while.
script.ja: ええ。妻がすごく心配するんです。非常用キットをもう一度見直すべきかもしれませんね。しばらく手をつけてないから。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: That's probably a good idea. My kids actually helped update ours recently. It's good to involve them.
script.ja: それは良い考えだと思うわ。うちの子たちは最近、うちのを更新するのを手伝ってくれたのよ。巻き込むのは良いことだわ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Oh, that's smart. I didn't think of that. They're probably more aware of what's needed than I am.
script.ja: ああ、それは賢いですね。思いつきませんでした。僕より必要なものをよく知っているかもしれません。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Maybe. And they mentioned Tokyo's Akihabara neighborhood is adding new 'smart trash cans'.
script.ja: そうね。それから、秋葉原に新しい『スマートゴミ箱』が設置されるって言ってたわ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Smart trash cans? What does that even mean? Do they talk to you? Like, 'Please dispose of your rubbish thoughtfully'?
script.ja: スマートゴミ箱？それってどういう意味ですか？話しかけてくるんですか？「ゴミは思慮深く捨ててください」とか？

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: No, I think they just compact the trash and notify when they're full. So fewer pickups are needed.
script.ja: いいえ、ゴミを圧縮して、満杯になったら通知するだけだと思うわ。だから回収の回数が減るのね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Oh, that's actually... practical. Akihabara can get pretty crowded, especially with tourists.
script.ja: ああ、それは実際に…実用的ですね。秋葉原は、特に観光客でかなり混雑しますから。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Yes, and the current bins are sometimes a bit sparse. This might help.
script.ja: ええ、それに今のゴミ箱は時々少し疎らなのよね。これは役立つかもしれないわ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Sparse? What does 'sparse' mean? Like, not many of them?
script.ja: 疎ら？「sparse」ってどういう意味ですか？あんまりない、みたいな？

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Exactly. 'Sparse' means there aren't many of something, or they're spread out thinly. Like 'few and far between'.
script.ja: その通りよ。「sparse」は、何かの数が少ないか、まばらに広がっている状態を指すの。「数も少なく、間隔も広い」といった感じね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Ah, I see. So, the trash cans are sparse now. Got it. And they're getting a new giant Gundam, too, right?
script.ja: ああ、なるほど。じゃあ、今はゴミ箱が疎らだと。分かりました。それと、新しい巨大なガンダムもできるんですよね？

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Yes, that was in the news too. A new life-size statue. After the one in December was removed.
script.ja: ええ、それもニュースに出てたわね。新しい等身大の像よ。12月に撤去された後のね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: That's cool. I want to see that. Maybe I can take the baby when he's a bit older. For... contemplation.
script.ja: それはかっこいいですね。見に行きたいな。もう少し大きくなったら、赤ちゃんを連れて行けるかもしれません。こう…瞑想のために。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Contemplation? For a giant robot?
script.ja: 瞑想？巨大ロボットに？

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Yeah, like, you just look at it and... think about things. Big things. What does 'contemplation' actually mean, Sarah?
script.ja: ええ、こう、ただそれを見て…物事を考えるんです。大きなことを。サラさん、「contemplation」って実際どういう意味ですか？

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: 'Contemplation' means deep, thoughtful consideration or meditation. So, thinking deeply about something.
script.ja: 「Contemplation」は、深く、思慮深く考えること、または瞑想を意味するわ。だから、何かについて深く考えることね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Ah, okay. So, deep thinking about Gundam. Got it. I'm always doing that.
script.ja: ああ、なるほど。じゃあ、ガンダムについて深く考える、と。分かりました。僕はいつもそうしてるんですけどね。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: I'm sure you are. Anyway, speaking of thinking, did you know today is World Diabetes Day?
script.ja: そうでしょうね。ところで、考えることといえば、今日が世界糖尿病デーだって知ってた？

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: World Diabetes Day? Oh, I didn't know that. What's that about?
script.ja: 世界糖尿病デー？ああ、知りませんでした。それって何ですか？

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It was established by the UN in 2006. It's to promote awareness for the prevention, treatment, and management of diabetes.
script.ja: 2006年に国連が制定したのよ。糖尿病の予防、治療、療養に対する意識を高めるためのものね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Ah, I see. Because it's a pretty serious disease, right? I know a guy at work who has it.
script.ja: ああ、なるほど。かなり深刻な病気ですもんね？職場で糖尿病の人がいます。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It is. The blue circle is its symbol. It's meant to raise awareness that diabetes takes a life every 10 seconds worldwide.
script.ja: そうよ。青い丸がそのシンボルなの。糖尿病が世界中で10秒に1人の命を奪っているという意識を高めるためのものよ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Wow, every 10 seconds? That's really high. We should probably all try to eat a bit healthier.
script.ja: うわ、10秒に1人ですか？それは本当に高いですね。みんなもう少し健康的に食べるように努力すべきかもしれません。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Definitely. My son's been on a sugar-free kick lately. Trying to avoid all the sweets.
script.ja: 間違いなくそうね。うちの息子は最近、シュガーフリーにはまっててね。お菓子を全部避けてるの。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: That's good. My little one just wants to eat everything. Especially anything I'm eating. It's a battle.
script.ja: それはいいですね。うちの小さいのは何でも食べたがります。特に僕が食べてるもの。戦いですよ。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: I remember those days. It gets a little easier.
script.ja: そういう時期もあったわね。もう少し楽になるわよ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: I hope so. Anyway, thanks for the info, Sarah. Always good to learn something new on The Daily Tanu-chan Show.
script.ja: だといいんですけどね。とにかく、情報ありがとうございます、サラさん。『The Daily Tanu-chan Show』で新しいことを学ぶのはいつもいいですね。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: You're welcome, Alex. Have a good day.
script.ja: どういたしまして、アレックス。良い一日を。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: You too. And I'm definitely getting another coffee.
script.ja: サラさんも。そして僕は絶対にもう一杯コーヒーを飲みます。
